items.q: If a patient is fit for dialysis, the definitive indication listed is:
items.exp: Indications: uremic symptoms (definitive); volume, K⁺, acidosis (relative). (Book p807)

items.q: All but one are the relative indications bracketed in red. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Relative indications: volume, K⁺, acidosis; uremic symptoms are the definitive indication. (Book p807)

items.q: Fill up: To create access, the named vessel connection is an AV ______ (6 weeks to mature).
items.exp: Create access: AV fistula (6 weeks to mature). (Book p807)

items.q: The AV fistula needs how long to mature?
items.exp: AV fistula: 6 weeks to mature. (Book p807)

items.q: A CKD patient has volume overload and serum potassium 6.4 mmol/L but no uremic symptoms. These indications are classified as:
items.exp: Indications: uremic symptoms (definitive); volume, K⁺, acidosis (relative). (Book p807)

items.q: Uremic symptoms are listed as a relative indication for dialysis.
opts: False — uremic symptoms are the definitive indication
True, but only after a week
items.exp: Uremic symptoms (definitive); volume, K⁺, acidosis (relative). (Book p807)
